text: Skimmed milk is soured with a mesophilic starter and a drop of rennet, the gel is cut into small cubes and cooked until the grains firm up, then the whey is drained and the grains are washed cold so they do not stay sour. The grains are then mixed with a cream dressing. Washing dilutes the lactose and lactic acid and chilling stops the curd souring further.

steps.note: The milk is soured by a starter that must not make gas or slime.
The curd is cut at about pH 4.8, then left to rest for 15–20 min.
The curd is raised 0.5 °C every 5 min for the first 30 min, then faster, over about 2 h; the heat stops the culture.
The grains are mixed with cream and salt, which together decide most of the flavour.

processing.text: Some blends also carry Streptococcus thermophilus. The culture must not be gassy or ropy; rennet goes in about 90 min after it. Industrial North American cottage cheese is often set by direct acid instead.
